lessons.claim: The lattice-period modulation of the probe force (stick-slip) is large, 35% of the mean (±36 kT/d). A single sample's noise, k*·ℓ_k = 248 kT/d, is larger than the signal (98) so it is invisible in the raw data and only emerges after **period folding** (making a phase from the position mod a_NN and averaging like phases together) reduces it 32-fold. The shape is a sawtooth -- force builds as it pushes a lattice row and is released as it goes over. ⚠️ The folding assumes 'the conditions are the same in every cell', but dislocations accumulate so the first cell differs from a later one (this effect may be mixed into the larger ±49 modulation seen with 17 lattice cells). 2 sanity checks passed: F_y = −5.4±4.4 (1.2σ) · the stationary-trap control F_x = +3.3±6.2 (0.5σ).
